subject: economics
topic: Financial institutions: Central Bank of Nigeria, commercial banks, capital and money markets

kept.q: Which of the following is a money market instrument commonly used by the Nigerian government to raise short-term funds?
kept.explanation: Treasury bills are short-term debt securities issued by government and traded in the money market. Debentures, ordinary shares and preference shares are long-term securities traded in the capital market.
kept.pidgin: Treasury bills na short-term paper wey government dey issue for money market. Debentures, ordinary shares and preference shares na long-term things wey dem dey trade for capital market.

kept.q: Which of the following best describes how commercial banks create credit in an economy?
options: Banks print new currency notes to meet customer withdrawal demand
Banks lend out a fraction of their deposits while keeping the rest as reserve, thereby expanding the total money supply
Banks transfer all customer deposits to the Central Bank for safekeeping
Banks exchange foreign currency for local currency on behalf of customers
kept.explanation: Commercial banks keep only a small fraction of deposits as reserve and lend out the rest. As this lent money is redeposited and relent, the total money supply in the economy expands, a process called credit creation.
kept.pidgin: Commercial banks go keep small part of the money as reserve, then dem go loan out the rest. As dis money dey enter and comot again, e dey increase the total money wey dey circulate - na so credit creation dey work.

q.q: A customer deposits ₦50,000 into a commercial bank. If the Central Bank of Nigeria fixes the cash reserve ratio at 20%, what is the maximum total increase in bank deposits (through credit creation) that can result from this single deposit, assuming banks lend out all excess reserves?
q.explanation: The money (deposit) multiplier equals 1 divided by the reserve ratio, which is 1/0.20 = 5. Multiplying the initial deposit by this multiplier gives 50,000 x 5 = ₦250,000 as the maximum total deposit expansion.
q.pidgin: The multiplier na 1 divide by the reserve ratio, wey be 1/0.20 = 5. If you multiply the first deposit (50,000) by 5, you go get ₦250,000 as the total money wey fit enter the system.
